claims.text: Heptavalent equine botulinum antitoxin (HBAT [A to G]) is available in the US.
claims.quote: A heptavalent equine botulinum antitoxin (HBAT [A to G]) is available in the United States; it replaces the older trivalent antitoxin (2).

claims.text: Doesn't inactivate toxin already bound at the NMJ, so preexisting neuro impairment can't be reversed rapidly.
claims.quote: Antitoxin does not inactivate toxin that is already bound at the neuromuscular junction; therefore, preexisting neurologic impairment cannot be reversed rapidly.

claims.text: May slow or halt further progression.
claims.quote: However, antitoxin may slow or halt further progression.

claims.text: Give ASAP after clinical dx; don't delay for culture or toxicology results.
claims.quote: Antitoxin should be given as soon as possible after clinical diagnosis and not delayed to await culture or toxicology results.

claims.text: Less likely to help if given > 72 hours after Sx onset.
claims.quote: Antitoxin is less likely to be of benefit if given > 72 hours after symptom onset.

claims.text: US: report pts to state health authorities, who request it from the CDC (the only source).
claims.quote: In the United States, all patients who require the antitoxin must be reported to state health authorities, who then request the antitoxin from the CDC, which is the only source; clinicians cannot obtain antitoxin directly from the CDC.

claims.text: Horse-serum derived: risk of anaphylaxis or serum sickness.
claims.quote: Because antitoxin is derived from horse serum, there is a risk of anaphylaxis or serum sickness.

claims.text: Infant botulism types A and B: human botulinum immune globulin (BabyBIG).
claims.quote: Human botulinum immune globulin (BabyBIG) is available for the treatment of infant botulism types A and B
